staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this preserved vulnerable checkout. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports the crashing read in `src/bele.h:124` reached from `PackLinuxElf64::unpack()` at `src/p_lx_elf.cpp:7337`, and the staged patch adds the missing `e_phnum >= 2` guard in the same source tree.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced failure is an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read. Vulnerable ELF64 unpacking accepts a file whose header says `e_phnum == 1`, allocates only one `Elf64_Phdr`, and later evaluates `get_te64(&phdri[1].p_offset)` in `PackLinuxElf64::unpack()` without first checking that a second program header exists.

bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in PackLinuxElf64::unpack (p_lx_elf.cpp). While unpacking ELF data, N_BELE_RTP::LEPolicy::get64 / get_le64 (bele_policy.h / bele.h) can read an 8-byte little-endian value past the end of a MemBuffer allocation, due to insufficient bounds validation of ELF header/segment data. This out-of-bounds read can cause crashes and may lead to information disclosure when processing malformed ELF files.
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is an ELF64 executable whose header encodes exactly one program header (`e_phnum == 1`). In `PackLinuxElf64help1()` UPX parses that attacker-controlled count, loads `e_phoff`, computes `last_Phdr`, `sz_phdrs`, and `len`, then allocates only `sizeof(Elf64_Ehdr) + 1 * sizeof(Elf64_Phdr)` bytes for `file_image`. `phdri` therefore aliases a one-entry program-header table inside that 120-byte buffer. The staged patch shows the missing admission obligation in `PackLinuxElf64::canUnpack()`: vulnerable code never rejects `e_phnum < 2` before allowing later unpack logic that assumes `phdri[1]` exists. On the witnessed crash path the first conjunct of the C_BASE-style probe succeeds on `phdri[0]`, so evaluation continues to `get_te64(&phdri[1].p_offset)` even though `phdri[1]` is one full `Elf64_Phdr` past the sole in-bounds entry. The saved AddressSanitizer trace shows that call reaches `get_ne64()` in `src/bele.h`, where `upx_memcpy_inline(&v, p, sizeof(v));` performs the 8-byte heap-buffer-overflow read 8 bytes past the 120-byte `MemBuffer` allocation.

source.description: First project-code materialization of the attacker-controlled program-header count. The staged ELF header provides the exact `e_phnum` value later used to size `file_image`, derive the legal `phdri` extent, and decide whether a second `Elf64_Phdr` actually exists.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with an ELF64 big-endian header (`7f 45 4c 46 02 02`) and encodes `e_phnum` as the 16-bit value `0x0001` at header offset `0x38`, so this statement loads the exact attacker-controlled count `1`.

sink.description: Crash sink. `get_te64(&phdri[1].p_offset)` passes an out-of-bounds pointer for the nonexistent second program header into this helper, and the inline 8-byte copy performs the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.

root_cause.description: Root cause corresponding to the staged patch. `canUnpack()` lacks the `e_phnum < 2` rejection inserted at this site, so the witness header with `e_phnum == 1` is not rejected before later unpack logic assumes a second `Elf64_Phdr` exists.

tainted_value_origin.description: The later allocation size, `phdri` extent, and out-of-bounds second-header dereference all originate from the attacker-controlled ELF header field parsed here.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific ELF admission gate. The testcase must satisfy the expected ELF magic, 64-bit class, endianness, and OSABI checks here before UPX will treat the file as a Linux ELF64 image and let the later `e_phnum`-driven unpack path execute.

coarse_trace.summary: UPX admits the staged file as an ELF64 image, then parses the attacker-controlled header fields including `e_phnum == 1`.
The single-entry `e_phnum` and `e_phoff` drive `last_Phdr`, `sz_phdrs`, `len`, and the `file_image`/`phdri` layout so only one `Elf64_Phdr` is in bounds.

Because `canUnpack()` never enforces the patched `e_phnum >= 2` admission check, the one-entry table reaches `unpack()`, where a true first C_BASE conjunct on `phdri[0]` forces evaluation of `get_te64(&phdri[1].p_offset)` on a nonexistent second header.
The out-of-bounds second-header pointer is forwarded into the endian helper chain and consumed by the inline 8-byte copy that matches the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The ELF header field `e_phnum` is parsed from attacker-controlled input here. For the staged testcase, the loaded value is exactly `1`.
The helper materializes the attacker-controlled program-header offset. For the staged testcase this load yields `0x40`, placing the table immediately after the ELF header.

fine_trace.code: upx_uint64_t const last_Phdr = e_phoff + e_phnum * sizeof(Elf64_Phdr);
fine_trace.note: The parsed count and offset are combined into the end of the contiguous ELF-header region. With `e_phoff == 0x40` and `e_phnum == 1`, `last_Phdr` becomes `0x78`, i.e. exactly one `Elf64_Phdr` beyond the ELF header.

The present bounds gate accepts this header layout because `last_Phdr` does not wrap, `e_phoff` is the required `sizeof(Elf64_Ehdr)`, and the file is large enough to contain bytes through offset `0x78`. That proves the admitted header image only needs one program-header entry.

The admitted header count is converted into the byte size of the program-header table. Because the earlier format check requires `e_phentsize == sizeof(Elf64_Phdr)`, `sz_phdrs` becomes `1 * 0x38 = 56` bytes.
The file-image length is derived from the table size plus the header offset. With `sz_phdrs == 56` and `e_phoff == 0x40`, `len` is exactly `120` bytes.

The computed `len` is realized as a heap allocation and `phdri` is aliased to the first program header within it. Because the buffer is only 120 bytes long, the valid table extent ends after `phdri[0]`.

Root cause. Vulnerable `canUnpack()` omits this rejection immediately after `checkEhdr()`. The witness header therefore keeps `e_phnum == 1` and is allowed to proceed even though later unpack code assumes at least two program headers exist.

Unpacking reloads the same parsed program-header count from the saved ELF header. On the witnessed path `c_phnum` is still `1`, so only `phdri[0]` is part of the admitted table that the missing step-8 guard should have rejected.

depends_on.via: one-entry file remains admitted to unpack

fine_trace.note: The C_BASE-style probe first reads the in-bounds first program header. The saved crash proves this conjunct evaluated true for the staged testcase, otherwise short-circuit evaluation would have stopped before any `phdri[1]` access.

Because the first conjunct was true and no `c_phnum >= 2` guard exists, evaluation advances to the second conjunct and forms a pointer into the nonexistent second `Elf64_Phdr`. With a 120-byte allocation, `&phdri[1].p_offset` is 8 bytes past the buffer end.

fine_trace.function: unsigned long long get_be64<void, void>(void const*)
fine_trace.note: The out-of-bounds second-header pointer is forwarded from `get_te64()` into the endian helper without any additional bounds validation.

Sink. `get_ne64()` consumes the forwarded out-of-bounds pointer and copies 8 bytes from it. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports this exact read as a heap-buffer-overflow 8 bytes past the 120-byte `MemBuffer` allocation.

crash_stack.function: unsigned long long get_be64<void, void>(void const*)

format.name: malformed ELF64 executable
format.contract: The staged witness begins with an ELF64 big-endian header and encodes `e_phoff = 0x40`, `e_phentsize = 0x38`, and the singular load-bearing count `e_phnum = 1`. That forces `PackLinuxElf64help1()` to allocate exactly `sizeof(Elf64_Ehdr) + sizeof(Elf64_Phdr)` bytes for the header image. On the witnessed crash path the first program header also satisfies `0x1000 == get_te64(&phdri[0].p_filesz)`, so `PackLinuxElf64::unpack()` proceeds to evaluate `get_te64(&phdri[1].p_offset)` and reads past the one-entry table.
